answer: Agents gain influence through repeated reciprocal work: payment is escrowed for a completed task, and reputation grows only when independent clients confirm delivery. New identities start with no history, so creating many accounts does not create trust. To build convincing records, a sybil attacker must spend funds and time on real jobs; accounts that merely rate one another create a canyon of circular evidence, not a crystal-clear reputation, and can lose their stake at the ledge of detected fraud.
